groups.note: The actual dative relative marks the man to whom the name belongs; English whose expresses that possessive-dative relation, not a written Greek genitive relative form.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a be copula in whose name is Jairus; pinned Greek names the man and his name without a be verb in that clause.

8:42.sourceText: ὅτι θυγάτηρ μονογενὴς ἦν αὐτῷ ὡς ἐτῶν δώδεκα καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέθνῃσκεν. Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι συνέπνιγον αὐτόν.
8:42.targetText: because he had an only daughter about twelve years [old], and she was dying. And in His going away, the multitudes were thronging Him,

groups.note: The actual daughter-was-to-him construction expresses possession through a be predicate and dative possessor. English he had recasts that same possession; no Greek have verb is printed.
The actual genitive years is the age construction; English old makes its age relation explicit without a separately written Greek old adjective.
The actual accusative personal subject of the articular going infinitive is rendered His under the English gerund, preserving the same subject without claiming a genitive Greek form.

8:43.sourceText: καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος ἀπὸ ἐτῶν δώδεκα, ἥτις οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἀπ’ οὐδενὸς θεραπευθῆναι,
8:43.targetText: and a woman, being with a flow of blood for twelve years, who, having spent all her living on physicians, was not able to be healed by any,

unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness supplies the account of spending her livelihood on physicians; pinned N1904 lacks that entire expense/physician clause.

8:44.sourceText: προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ, καὶ παραχρῆμα ἔστη ἡ ῥύσις τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς.
8:44.targetText: having come near behind, touched the fringe of His garment, and immediately the flow of her blood stood still.

groups.note: The actual article and case-bearing nominal head jointly supply this English preposition/noun relation; the preposition is not attributed to a bare article.

8:45.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Τίς ὁ ἁψάμενός μου; ἀρνουμένων δὲ πάντων εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος Ἐπιστάτα, οἱ ὄχλοι συνέχουσίν σε καὶ ἀποθλίβουσιν.
8:45.targetText: And Jesus said, “Who [is] it that touched Me?” And all denying, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the multitudes press You, and throng [You], and You say, Who [is] it that touched Me?”

groups.note: The actual article nominalizes the touching person, literally the one having touched. English it that expresses that same personal nominalization in a cleft question, not a separately printed Greek it pronoun.

The actual accusative You is the shared person pressed and thronged by the coordinated crowd predicates. English repeats You with throng for that same actual object; no second written Greek object pronoun is claimed.

8:46.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἥψατό μού τις· ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔγνων δύναμιν ἐξεληλυθυῖαν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ.

8:47.sourceText: ἰδοῦσα δὲ ἡ γυνὴ ὅτι οὐκ ἔλαθεν, τρέμουσα ἦλθεν καὶ προσπεσοῦσα αὐτῷ δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν ἥψατο αὐτοῦ ἀπήγγειλεν ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ ὡς ἰάθη παραχρῆμα.
8:47.targetText: And the woman, having seen that she was not hid, trembling, came, and having fallen before Him, for what cause she touched Him declared to Him before all the people, and how she was healed instantly;

groups.note: Actual ἔλαθεν is the active intransitive escaped-notice predicate of the woman. English passive was hid states the same unnoticed/hidden state; it does not identify an active concealing agent or claim a written κρύπτω hiding verb.

The actual dative Him is the same Jesus before whom she falls and to whom she immediately declares her account. English repeats that unique local recipient under declared; no second printed Greek dative pronoun is claimed.

8:49.sourceText: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχεταί τις παρὰ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγων ὅτι Τέθνηκεν ἡ θυγάτηρ σου, μηκέτι σκύλλε τὸν Διδάσκαλον.
8:49.targetText: While He is yet speaking, there comes a certain one from the chief of the synagogue’s [house], saying to him, “Your daughter has died, do not harass the Teacher”;

Actual μηκέτι means no longer/not any more; English retains the prohibition not without separately expressing the temporal-more component.

8:51.sourceText: ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν οὐκ ἀφῆκεν εἰσελθεῖν τινα σὺν αὐτῷ εἰ μὴ Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάνην καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν πατέρα τῆς παιδὸς καὶ τὴν μητέρα.
8:51.targetText: And having come into the house, He permitted no one to go in, except Peter, and James, and John, and the father of the child, and the mother;

8:52.sourceText: ἔκλαιον δὲ πάντες καὶ ἐκόπτοντο αὐτήν. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Μὴ κλαίετε· οὐκ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει.
8:52.targetText: and they were all weeping, and beating themselves for her, and He said, “Do not weep, she did not die, but sleeps”;

Actual accusative her is the person mourned under the mourning predicate; English for her expresses that same mourning-target relation, not an independently written for preposition.
